metadata.title: Gino: Knife Throw, Every Feature, Played
metadata.audience: makers following the channel's Claude + Walker game workflows
metadata.note: godot-waikthrough walker film. Every gameplay beat is an exact-frame window of a scripted-input take of the real game; no human playtest. Game audio was not captured; narration only. No paid calls, no upload.

beats.narration_text: Hola, this is Liam, in for Bear. This is how Walker is meant to be asked: a game design document in, a playable Godot project out. The prompt is a reconstruction. This game was a Unity platformer with scripts and art but no levels, rebuilt in Godot with three.

props.command: Please use Walker to convert my game design document about a 2D action platformer — guide Gino home through three hostile valleys with a sword combo, three throwing knives and three hearts — into a playable Godot project.
props.runningText: illustrative reconstruction — not the historical prompt
output: Built: 3 levels, 3 enemy types, 14 scripts and a shader.
Played here: 3 scripted-input takes, 46 of 46 assertions passing.

beats.narration_text: Gino: Knife Throw is a side-scrolling action platformer: a sword combo, three knives, three hearts, and a door at the end of each level. Every feature here is played through real key, mouse and gamepad input, by a script. Nobody has played it by hand yet.

props.text:
Gino: Knife Throw
is an endless runner.
Three levels and a door.

The full four-hit combo, with the magic blast as its fourth hit, never appears in these takes, because each hit knocks the enemy back out of reach. The game's own playtest checks the four-hit chain, off screen. A dagger, the bat, and the spike hint.

beats.narration_text: Verdict. Every level, the credits, defeat and retry play through real input, and forty-six assertions pass. Two defects: level three's bridge has a hole at one end, and R on a menu logs a script error. And the script finished level three on half a heart. Whether that's tense or unfair is a person's call.

artifactLines: Observed: menu → 3 levels → credits → Continue; and pit → game over → retry.
Checks: 46 of 46 film-capture assertions pass; the game's own playtest passes.
Defects: a 16 px hole at the end of level 3's bridge; R logs a SCRIPT ERROR (level.gd:761).
Untested: a human playtest, the four-hit combo on screen, Windows, game audio.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude in your own Godot project: Use Walker on my Godot game. Write an input-only capture script that plays one feature through real key and mouse events, asserts what should happen on screen, and fails loudly if it doesn't. Then tell me one thing the capture can't prove. That last part matters: a script that wins is not a player who had fun. Liam, in for Bear.
